tools.name: read_source_member
tools.description: Download an IBM i source member as clean UTF-8 into a local editable copy, plus a pristine backup. Returns the saved paths and metadata, not the source text: read the saved file to see the code.

server.description: which IBM i to use, named by a .env.<name> file. Omit for the default .env server (see list_servers)

tools.name: search_source
tools.description: Grep the CODE of the members in a library, returning the matching lines with their sequence numbers. Still the slow tool, so scope it with sourceFile or memberType. To find a member by its name or its TEXT description instead, use list_members with a filter, which is a single query.

searchTerm.description: literal string to find in the source lines (not a regex)

sourceFile.description: limit to one source file, e.g. QDDSSRC

memberType.description: limit to a member type, e.g. DSPF, RPGLE

server.description: which IBM i to use, named by a .env.<name> file. Omit for the default .env server (see list_servers)

tools.name: list_libraries
tools.description: List libraries (schemas) on the IBM i with their text descriptions, so you can discover where source lives before drilling in with list_source_files and list_members. Lists user libraries by default. Pass filter to narrow by a substring of the library name or its description, e.g. a project or application name.

filter.description: substring to match against the library name or its text, ignoring case. Omit to list all user libraries.

includeSystem.description: also include the IBM Q* system libraries (default false, user libraries only)

server.description: which IBM i to use, named by a .env.<name> file. Omit for the default .env server (see list_servers)

tools.name: manage_library_list
tools.description: View or change the connection's library list. `show` returns the current list (SYSTEM/PRODUCT/CURRENT/USER portions). `add` and `remove` add or drop one library (ADDLIBLE/RMVLIBLE), `set_current` sets the current library (CHGCURLIB), and `replace` sets the whole user portion (CHGLIBL). Changes last for the session and are used by later compiles, like adding a library on the green screen. It only changes the job's library list, never objects or data. Use this when a compile needs a library that is not on the sign on list. The change actions are disabled when IBMI_READ_ONLY is set, while `show` always works.

action.description: show the list, add/remove one library, set the current library, or replace the whole user portion

library.description: the library for add, remove, or set_current

libraries.description: the full user library list for replace, in search order (first = highest priority)

position.description: for add: put it first (searched first) or last (default)

currentLibrary.description: for replace: also set the current library

server.description: which IBM i to use, named by a .env.<name> file. Omit for the default .env server (see list_servers)

tools.name: list_source_files
tools.description: List the source physical files in a library (e.g. QRPGLESRC, QDDSSRC) with their text descriptions. Use to explore where source lives before listing members.

server.description: which IBM i to use, named by a .env.<name> file. Omit for the default .env server (see list_servers)

tools.name: list_members
tools.description: Browse members in a library (like PDM/RDi): each member with its name, type, and TEXT description. Omit sourceFile to list across all source files. Pass filter to find a member by its purpose without reading any code: it matches a substring of the member name or its TEXT description in one query, so it is the fast way in (e.g. a Dutch word like 'afdeling'). Use search_source only when you need to match the code itself.

sourceFile.description: limit to one source file, e.g. QDDSSRC

memberType.description: limit to a type, e.g. DSPF

filter.description: substring to match against the member name or its text description, ignoring case. Omit to list everything.

server.description: which IBM i to use, named by a .env.<name> file. Omit for the default .env server (see list_servers)

tools.name: upload_source_member
tools.description: Upload a local file into a source member on the IBM i. By default this reads, modifies and writes back a member that already exists, defaulting to the copy read_source_member wrote. For brand new development, where the member does not exist yet, pass create: true and the member is added first (addpfm) with the right source type. Creation is opt in so a mistyped member name cannot leave a stray member behind in a customer library.

localPath.description: path to the edited file, defaults to the local copy from read_source_member

content.description: upload this text directly instead of reading a file

create.description: create the member first if it does not exist yet (addpfm). Default false: uploading into a member that is not there fails instead, so a typo cannot create one.

memberType.description: source type used when creating, e.g. DSPF, SQLRPGLE, RPGLE, PF, CLLE. Defaults to the local file's extension, since read_source_member names copies <member>.<type>. Required when creating from `content`. Worth passing explicitly: the type decides which command compile_member picks.

text.description: member text description, shown in PDM next to the member. Used only when creating. Max 50 characters.

server.description: which IBM i to use, named by a .env.<name> file. Omit for the default .env server (see list_servers)

tools.name: compile_member
tools.description: Compile a source member and return whether it succeeded, the compiler listing, and structured errors. Built-in command per type, override with `command`.

targetLibrary.description: where the object is created, default *curlib. Pass a real library to also get structured EVFEVENT errors.

objectName.description: compiled object name, defaults to the member name

type.description: override the detected member type, e.g. RPGLE

server.description: which IBM i to use, named by a .env.<name> file. Omit for the default .env server (see list_servers)

tools.name: list_servers
tools.description: List the configured IBM i servers you can target with the `server` parameter. The default server is `.env`, and each additional `.env.<name>` file adds a server named <name>.
